root_cause.text: The i.MX8MQ VPU block controller driver incorrectly modeled the VPUMIX ADB as having separate per-domain reset/clock bits for G1 and G2, even though that hardware is reset and ungated only together with the VPU, so the driver could attempt an invalid separate reset that hangs the system.
root_cause.evidence: The patch comment states that “the ADB in the VPUMIX domain has no separate reset and clock enable bits, but is ungated and reset together with the VPUs” and that “Resetting G1 or G2 separately may led to system hang,” then removes `rst_mask = BIT(1)/BIT(0)` and `clk_mask = BIT(1)/BIT(0)` from `imx8mq_vpu_blk_ctl_domain_data[]` for G1 and G2.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix i.MX8MQ VPU power-domain handling by preventing separate G1/G2 reset/clock control and delegating reset to the shared VPU notifier to avoid system hangs.
intent_record.what: The comment above the i.MX8MQ VPU block control domain table was expanded to explain that the ADB in the VPUMIX domain shares reset/clock control with the VPUs and that resetting G1 or G2 independently can hang the system. In the `imx8mq_vpu_blk_ctl_domain_data` array, the `rst_mask` and `clk_mask` fields were removed from both the `IMX8MQ_VPUBLK_PD_G1` and `IMX8MQ_VPUBLK_PD_G2` entries.
intent_record.how: By clearing the reset and clock masks for the G1 and G2 domains, the per-domain block controller no longer tries to reset or ungate those subdomains separately. This shifts reset handling to `imx8mq_vpu_power_notifier()`, which performs the actual VPU reset in the intended shared manner and avoids the hang caused by independent G1/G2 resets.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly matches the root cause: it fixes the incorrect per-domain G1/G2 reset/clock handling for the i.MX8MQ VPU by using the shared VPU reset path, which addresses the invalid separate reset that could hang the system.

candidates.rationale: This models G1 as having its own reset bit, which is the core incorrect assumption behind attempting separate reset control for a domain that should only reset with the shared VPU.
This assigns a dedicated clock gate bit to G1, reinforcing the incorrect per-domain control model for the VPU block and enabling invalid separate ungating/reset behavior.
This models G2 as having its own reset bit, which is the same root cause: treating a shared hardware reset as independently controllable per domain.
This assigns a separate clock gate bit to G2, contributing to the invalid split of shared VPU hardware control into per-domain bits.

vuln_statements.explanation: This line incorrectly gives the G1 domain its own reset bit, but the VPU hardware reset is shared and must not be controlled separately. That mistaken per-domain reset modeling is the root cause of the invalid reset attempt that can hang the system.

This line assigns a dedicated clock gate bit to G1, reinforcing the invalid assumption that the VPU block can be controlled independently per domain. That contributes to the separate ungate/reset behavior that is unsafe for this hardware.
This line incorrectly gives the G2 domain its own reset bit even though the reset is shared across the VPU block. That erroneous independent reset control is part of the vulnerability.

This line assigns a separate clock gate bit to G2, which is part of the same incorrect split of shared VPU control into per-domain control. It enables the invalid separate ungating/reset handling behind the bug.
